en: The Apadāna of the Elder Phusitakampiya Gandhodaka Chapter, Number 5 I was once a king named Kappina, ruling over a realm of four continents. At that time, the Buddha Vipassi appeared in the world. Having heard of his fame, I went to him with a retinue of eighty-four thousand. I offered him a great rain of perfumed water and, having paid homage, I sat to one side. As I sat there, the Blessed One preached the Dhamma to me; at the conclusion of that discourse, I attained the fruit of stream-entry. Having passed away from that life, I was reborn in the Tusita heaven. From Tusita, I passed away and was reborn in the human world. There, I became a wheel-turning monarch, a sovereign of the four continents, endowed with the seven treasures and possessing the four bases of power. In this final existence, I was born into a noble family. When I had grown up, I went forth into homelessness under the dispensation of the Buddha Kassapa. For twenty thousand years, I practiced the holy life under the Teacher Kassapa. Having fulfilled my duties, I passed away and was reborn in the Brahma-world. From Brahma, I passed away and was reborn in the human world. There, I became a wheel-turning monarch, a sovereign of the four continents, endowed with the seven treasures and possessing the four bases of power. In this final existence, I was born into a noble family. When I had grown up, I went forth into homelessness under the dispensation of the Buddha Gotama. Having seen the Buddha, the World-Honored One, I offered him a rain of perfumed water. Because of that deed, I have now attained the state of an Arhat. My mind is liberated, and I am free from all defilements. I have reached the end of suffering. This is my final birth. I shall not be born again. This is the Apadāna of the Elder Phusitakampiya.
“The Fully Enlightened One named Vipassī,
the eldest in the world, the bull among men,
was accompanied by those whose taints were destroyed.”
He was then dwelling in the monastery.
Having emerged from the gate of the monastery,
Vipassī, the Leader of the World, [proceeded].
Together with one hundred thousand [beings] and eight who were free from taints, he was there;
I myself was clothed in a deerskin.
And though wearing garments of bark,
taking flowers and water,
I approached the Perfectly Enlightened One.
Having gladdened his own mind,
filled with joy and with palms joined,
he took water mixed with flowers.
I showered the Buddha with [flowers].
By that kamma, the Fully Enlightened One named Jalajuttama [was born].
Having proclaimed my deed,
he went to where he had aspired.
Five thousand raindrops fell.
With those two thousand five hundred [attendants], I honored the Jina;
I exercised divine sovereignty over two thousand five hundred [worlds].
With two thousand five hundred [followers],
I was a wheel-turning monarch;
by the remainder of my karma—
I attained the state of an Arhat.
Whether I was a king of the gods or a lord of men;
That very name of mine remains;
I am indeed named Phusita.
While I was existing as a deva, I remained so.
Or even for a human being,
it rains upon me from all sides to the distance of a fathom, like a fine spray.
The states of existence have been uprooted by me;
my defilements have been incinerated;
all taints are completely exhausted.
This is the fruit of my sprinkling:
from my body, just as from sandalwood,
a fragrance wafts forth.
From my body, a fragrance wafts for half a league;
it emits a divine scent.
Having smelled the fragrance of those endowed with meritorious deeds, they know:
"Phusita has arrived here."
The branches, leaves, and wood,
and even all the grasses—
having understood my intention, they [acted].
At that moment, a fragrance arose.
A hundred thousand eons ago,
I made offerings of sandalwood.
I do not know a state of woe;
this is the fruit of sprinkling.
The four analytical knowledges—
the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed did the venerable elder Phusitakampiya speak these verses.
The legend of the Elder Phusitakampiya is the fifth.
